newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: POLYGRAM MUSIC SALES UP ON RELEASE SCHEDULE.
newsitem.headline: POLYGRAM MUSIC SALES UP ON RELEASE SCHEDULE.

text.p: Music and entertainment group PolyGram NV said on Tuesday its first quarter music sales rose nine percent, boosted by a stronger release schedule, while overall sales were helped by a strong dollar and sterling.
PolyGram, 75 percent owned by Philips Electronics NV , reports in guilders which have weakened substantially against both currencies.

"A stronger music release schedule contributed to sales growth of nine percent in Europe and 12 percent in North America," the company said in a statement with results, its first quarterly announcement.

The new album "Pop" from Irish rockers U2, which was delayed from last year and released in March, sold nearly five million units worldwide during the period, making it the company's best seller in the quarter.

Operating margins at the unit, which a spokeswoman said were up to 13.1 percent in the period from 12.1 percent in the first quarter of 1996, also benefited from strong releases from the Bee Gees, Warren G and Texas, PolyGram said.
Local artists such as Andrea Bocelli in Italy and Marco Borsato in the Netherlands also made a strong contribution, with Bocelli selling over two million albums in the first quarter.
Releases from 1996 which carried over well into 1997 included albums from Sheryl Crow, Foxy Brown, Zucchero as well as soundtracks from "Grease" and "Shine".
For the remainder of 1997 PolyGram said it was expecting new albums from established artists such as Wet Wet Wet, INXS, Jon Bon Jovi, Boyz II Men and Elton John.
